paragraphs: Seder HaDorot brings a wondrous story about him, which its compiler copied from a small book of tales. Hyman says that since it is not found in the Midrash, “we have not copied it.”[^1]

notes.text: בסה״ד is contextually Seder HaDorot, with machine בסה״ר versus supplied בסה״ד retained as provenance. והעתיק is active; its compiler is the natural but unstated subject, not a newly identified author. The small book of tales has no precise supplied title; the Midrash is likewise unspecified. Hyman’s first-person-plural לא העתקנו is represented as his decision not to copy, and the negative source observation is not a fresh exhaustive search. The sole personal-title abbreviation remains R'.
